subject: Mid-quarter trajectory update — scope rebalancing & critical dependency asks
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Hugh Chen <hugh.chen@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-quarter trajectory update — scope rebalancing & critical dependency asks

Team —

Quick mid-quarter pulse ahead of next week’s QBR prep: overall progress on our Q3 serving & cost-reduction OKRs is roughly 42% of target throughput increases with material variance across initiatives. The goal of this note is to call out three things we need to lock before the QBR: 1) explicit re-scopes on two initiatives to protect runway, 2) owners for cross-team dependencies that are currently unowned, and 3) a short list of ask items we can present to execs for targeted approvals.

High-level status (concise):
- Serving runtime throughput (OKR-1): 48% progress. Early kernels landed but perf gaps remain for long-context flows.
- Cost/unit reduction (OKR-2): 39% progress. Savings on batching are on track; KV cache misses still costly.
- Dedicated capacity adoption (OKR-3): 40% progress. Two pilot customers live; we need a simplified onboarding doc.

Proposed scope rebalances (I recommend we present these as ‘protecting runway’ moves):
- A: Defer non-critical mobile model quantization work (2 sprints) — reassign 0.6 FTE from quantization to runtime kernel fixes.
- B: Narrow the telemetry ingestion proof-of-concept to sampling-based metrics (deliver core signal this quarter; full fidelity next quarter).

Critical unowned dependencies (need named owners by EOD Mon Aug 10):
- Cross-region failover test plan (automation infra) — currently no owner.
- Customer migration checklist for Dedicated (documentation + billing hooks) — needs a PM + engineer.
- Legal signoff on limited-data retention exception for pilot partners (Hugh C. is copied as an external stakeholder).

Attachments: QBR_prep_deck_v2.pdf (deck draft), tech-deps-snapshot.xlsx (current dependency spreadsheet).

Asks: please reply with owners + a quick note if you disagree with the two recommended re-scopes. If you have other high-impact items to surface to the execs, add them inline. I’ll consolidate and circulate a one-page ask for the QBR by Tue morning.

Thanks —
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks for the clear callout. Quick responses inline: 

- I agree with Re-scope A (defer non-critical mobile quant). We’ll reassign 0.6 FTE from quantization to kernel fixes; I can name lead: Kevin Park (eng) will own the kernel work.
- For the cross-region failover test plan: I can take ownership for the test plan delivery but need infra automation support from SRE. Can we ask SRE to commit a single sprint for test harnessing? I’ll put together a minimal plan by Mon EOD.
- Customer migration checklist: Marissa, can you lead doc + billing hooks? I can help with the onboarding checklist items for Dedicated.
- Legal signoff: tagging Hugh here is good — Legal will need the limited-data retention proposal and a list of customers affected.

I’ve attached a short note with proposed sprint assignments and the names I suggest for each role (will upload to the Drive). If everyone agrees, I’ll update the tech-deps sheet with owners and estimated effort.

Vanessa Ortiz
